item.title: Virtual electrode XPS experiments on Li3−xSc1−xZrxCl6 (x ∼ 0.2): Oxygen-mediated interface passivation on metallic lithium anodes
item.description: Lithium metal chlorides are a promising class of solid-state electrolyte (SSE) materials that may enable the use of lithium anodes for next-generation electrochemical energy storage. Zr-substituted Li3ScCl6 (Li3-xSc1-xZrxCl6), combines the high ionic conductivities of Li3ScCl6 with the moisture resistance of Li2ZrCl6 that facilitates processing and manufacturing. However, little is known about the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) formation and composition at the Li3-xSc1-xZrxCl6 and Li metal anode interfacial region. Elucidating the relevant (electro)chemical processes is crucial for engineering Li3-xSc1-xZrxCl6 | Li0 interfaces with low interfacial impedances and long-term cycling stability. Here, we utilize the virtual-electrode X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (VE-XPS) technique study the formation and early-stage evolution of the SEI. Additionally, we investigate the long-term effects of galvanostatic cycling on the ion transport properties and how SEI evolution impacts the overall electrochemical impedance of Li2.8Sc0.8Zr0.2Cl6-based cells. Our results show the initial SEI formation diverges from thermodynamic phase decomposition predictions due to the presence of oxygen, leading to formation of a novel Li-Sc-Zr-oxide (LSZO) phase that is compositionally similar to Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO). For the early-stage SEI, this oxygen-mediated decomposition pathway appears to mitigate reduction of the metal cations and prevent the formation of metallic phases (e.g., metallic Zr, Sc, and Sc-Zr alloys). We find that LSZO phase formation effectively passivates the Li2.8Sc0.8Zr0.2Cl6 | Li0 interface and enables plating and stripping of metallic lithium.

item.title: TCSP3.0: Template-Based Crystal Structure Prediction with Coefficient-Preserving Element Substitution and Structural Diversity
item.description: arXiv:2610.34029v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Template-based crystal structure prediction (CSP) transfers a known crystal structure to a new composition by element substitution, so its accuracy depends on retrieving suitable templates, mapping elements and ranking the resulting candidates correctly. Auditing the original TCSP2.0 implementation on the T180 benchmark, we found that 469 of its 2,347 selected structures (20%) have the wrong composition, caused by element mappings that ignore stoichiometric coefficients and by sequential text substitution that cascades or corrupts element symbols. We propose TCSP3.0, which enforces coefficient-preserving mappings, substitutes species simultaneously on parsed structures and validates every candidate's composition and cell. It further adds periodic-number retrieval, soft oxidation-state evidence, radius-compatibility scoring, structural deduplication, and ORB-v3 machine-learning-potential relaxation and energy ranking of its candidates, as used by deep generative CSP baselines. TCSP3.0 achieves Top-1 and Top-20 match rates of 72.2% and 90.6% on T180, compared with 28.3% and 45.6% for TCSP2.0, and a Top-20 match rate of 74.0% on a new 800-target benchmark (T800). On T180 it also outperforms PNcsp+ and deep generative models CrystalFlow and MaskGXT (Top-1 72.2% versus at most 63.9%). Even without relaxation, TCSP3.0 reaches 67.8% at Top-1 and 90.6% at Top-20 in a median of 28 s per target on two CPU cores, about ten times faster than CrystalFlow. Paired ten-arm ablations on T180 and T800 show that most of the improvement comes from the correctness fixes; structural deduplication significantly improves the Top-5 match rate, embedding-based retrieval is required for coverage, and the remaining scoring features have small or null effects.

item.title: Phase fluctuations dominated superconductivity in a thick Granular Boron-Doped Diamond film
item.description: arXiv:2610.34319v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the superconducting properties of a 1.2-{\mu}m-thick granular boron-doped diamond film, where tightly packed grains form a disordered network of Josephson junctions. The film exhibits a sharp superconducting transition at a critical temperature, T_c ~ 3 K. Its transport properties are well described by the Ambegaokar-Halperin theory of phase fluctuations. Direct measurements of the penetration depth using a two-coil mutual inductance technique reveal classic phase-fluctuation-dominated behavior: below T_c, the superfluid density (n_s) varies linearly over a wide temperature range - a hallmark of thermal phase fluctuations - before crossing over to a T^2 dependence at ultra-low temperatures. Both the large low-temperature penetration depth, {\lambda}(0) ~ 8.8 {\mu}m, and the slope of the linear ns variation in the thermal regime reveal a remarkably low superfluid stiffness in the range of 0.5-0.8 K. These results establish granular boron-doped diamond films as an excellent model system for investigating the role of long-wavelength phase fluctuations in three-dimensional superconductors.

item.title: Fermionic superfluid transition and pairing scale separation in the kagome flat band
item.description: arXiv:2610.34342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flat-band systems provide a promising platform for exploring exotic correlated phases owing to quenched kinetic energy and enhanced interaction effects. In this work, we investigate the flat-band superfluid transition in the attractive kagome Hubbard model using large-scale determinant quantum Monte Carlo simulations accelerated by fast Fourier transforms and delay updates. Through systematic calculations of the transition temperature, spin susceptibility, and density compressibility, we establish the finite-temperature phase diagram at the flat-band filling $\rho=5/3$ and find a clear linear scaling of the superfluid transition temperature with the interaction strength, $T_{\mathrm{c}}=0.0314|U|$. Our results reveal a wide separation of temperature scales between local pair formation and global phase coherence, which stabilizes a broad intermediate supercompressible bosonic fluid region of preformed pairs that bridges the normal Fermi gas and the flat-band superfluid. We further demonstrate that both the transition temperature and density compressibility are significantly enhanced in the flat band compared to van Hove fillings. Our findings highlight the essential role of flat-band-enhanced pair-density fluctuations in separating the pairing and phase-coherence scales, offering clear experimental signatures for probing flat-band superfluidity and superconductivity in cold-atom and kagome-material platforms.

item.title: Phase field dislocation dynamics prediction of stacking fault widths in Cu-Al Alloys using generalised stacking fault energy from DFT and interatomic potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34420v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The equilibrium width of intrinsic stacking faults is an important material parameter affecting key deformation phenomena. Here, we perform a comparative assessment of $\gamma$-surfaces generated using MD -- with a classical embedded-atom potential (ZW) and a machine-learned Gaussian Approximation Potential (GAP) -- and density functional theory (DFT), for Cu-Al alloys of varying Al content, and incorporate them as an energy term in PFDD simulations to obtain the equilibrium SFW. All three methods reproduce the lattice parameter and elastic moduli of Cu and Cu-Al alloys in reasonable agreement with each other and with experimental measurements from literature, but the MD-derived $\gamma$-surfaces, for both ZW and GAP, deviate substantially from DFT at the seven characteristic points, with the largest discrepancies at $T$ and $T_1$. When incorporated into PFDD, the DFT-derived $\gamma$-surfaces successfully predict an equilibrium SFW that increases with Al content and agrees well with standalone MD measurements and experimental values for pure Cu, whereas the MD-derived $\gamma$-surfaces do not yield an accurate SFW within PFDD, as the altered generalized stacking fault energy landscape causes the dissociating partials to become pinned soon after separation. These results show that DFT-derived $\gamma$-surfaces remain the more reliable route to alloy SFW prediction, and interatomic potentials must capture the shear path accurately to enable robust, efficient MD-PFDD modelling of stacking faults in alloys.

item.title: Computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chloride solid-state electrolytes
item.description: arXiv:2610.34505v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Amorphous solid-state electrolytes (SSEs) are attractive candidates for safe, high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries. The recent discovery that amorphous LiTaCl$_6$ and LiNbCl$_6$ reach room-temperature ionic conductivities above 10 mS cm$^{-1}$ with activation energies below 0.2 eV has spurred a broad search for new amorphous halide Li conductors. Here we report a computational screening of amorphous lithium trivalent-metal chlorides (Li-M(III)-Cl) using molecular dynamics driven by a universal machine-learning force field. For the sixteen Li-M(III)-Cl compositions spanning fifteen rare-earth elements and indium, all phases exhibit fast room-temperature Li$^+$ diffusion, with diffusivities of roughly $2$-$5 \times 10^{-7}$ cm$^2$ s$^{-1}$. After scaling the conductivity versus diffusivity relation to an experimental LiTaCl$_6$ reference, the estimated room-temperature conductivities range from 7.7 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$InCl$_6$ to 14 mS cm$^{-1}$ for amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$. With a low activation energy of 0.18 eV, amorphous Li$_3$ScCl$_6$ is predicted to be among the most conductive amorphous halide electrolytes. To rationalize the composition-dependent transport, we identify two descriptors: the Li$^+$ vibrational density of states (VDOS) center, which correlates inversely with diffusivity, and the average number of correlated bodies in string-like Li$^+$ motion. Compositions in which Li$^+$ has a lower VDOS center and migrates more by individual hopping rather than by concerted motion exhibit higher Li-ion diffusivities. These results suggest rich Li-ion transport characteristics in amorphous halide SSEs.

item.title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
item.description: arXiv:2610.34551v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning interatomic potentials enable atomistic simulations with near \textit{ab initio} accuracy over large length and time scales. Foundation models extend this capability across the periodic table but inherit the thermodynamic description of the electronic structure methods used to generate their training data. Small errors in relative phase stability can therefore produce large errors in transformation temperatures. We introduce an additive thermodynamic correction layer that shifts phase free energies towards an assessed reference without retraining or modifying the base potential. A first order thermodynamic construction converts the required phase free energy shifts directly into configuration energy targets, which are fitted using a linear atomic cluster expansion and refined iteratively from measured free energies. We apply the method to melting and solid to solid transformations across elements with different crystal structures using a foundation GRACE model. After the correction, all transformation temperatures lie within the prescribed tolerance of the assessed values, including Ca, Ti, and Zr, where a solid to solid transition and melting are corrected together. Static energy curves, bulk moduli, and liquid structure remain close to those of the base model. Vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density depend on the corrected phase balance and change where the correction is large. The method requires neither retraining, differentiable dynamics, nor access to the parameters of the base potential. It provides a modular route for combining transferable atomistic models with assessed phase thermodynamics.

item.title: From Autonomous Knowledge Generation to Generalizable Property Prediction: A Precision-First Pipeline for Electro-Optic Materials Discovery
item.description: arXiv:2610.34628v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Electro-optic materials, whose refractive index changes linearly with an applied electric field (the Pockels effect), set the speed and energy of optical modulators and microwave-to-optical links for quantum computing. Designing better materials requires optimizing composition alongside temperature, strain, and bias field. However, general repositories lack electro-optic tensor data. We present a pipeline that builds such a database from literature following the rule: "no value is better than a wrong value." The pipeline has five stages: physics-aware acquisition, layout-aware extraction via LLM and deterministic table parsers, a three-tier verification gate, cross-paper consensus using median and median absolute deviation, and a noise-robust surrogate model audited by leave-one-material-out (LOMO) testing. Physics enters directly: notation is mapped, point-group symmetry-forbidden Pockels components are rejected, equivalent labels are merged, and values carry provenance tags. In a run over 49 publications, the gate processed 816 candidates into 414 accepted, 215 held for review, and 187 rejected. Against a hand-certified gold standard of 303 values from 16 papers, the run achieved a precision of 0.51 and recall of 0.48 for exact record matches. Across four database snapshots, held-out materials where the surrogate model beat a predict-the-mean baseline grew from 1 of 4 to 9 of 13 as the database expanded from 10 to 22 materials. While not a controlled comparison, this trend supports the premise that a precision-oriented, physics-checked database can power forward models beyond its training set and clarifies requirements for inverse material design.

item.title: No Value Is Better Than a Wrong Value: Finding and Handling Erroneous Data in Literature-Mined Datasets for AI
item.description: arXiv:2610.34642v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning across materials science, chemistry, energy, and medicine increasingly relies on literature-extracted datasets due to a lack of curated databases. However, automated extraction introduces errors: text recognition misreads digits, units and notations are confused, values are misattributed, and LLMs hallucinate numbers. Drawing on our work building an electro-optic property database, we present a taxonomy of errors organized by their origin and signatures, alongside a layered framework for error detection. The framework combines schema and provenance checks, physical admissibility (bounds, symmetry, and governing equations), cross-source statistical consensus, model auditing, and suspicion-ranked review. In a production run, our verification gate halted 402 of 816 candidate values with typed reasons. Yet, an audit against curated references showed that 30 of 112 accepted values were defective; standard symmetry rules alone caught 21 of these. On measured BaTiO3 and KNbO3 tensors, constitutive identities caught 8 of 10 single-value errors and isolated the corrupted entries. In a controlled benchmark, the combined framework caught 81% of errors at 85% precision, including errors in single-report materials, bringing model accuracy on held-out data to within 3% of a model trained on clean data. Uncleaned data severely impairs discovery: 89% of the twenty largest values were errors, causing AI searches to prioritize false positives. Once bad numbers are controlled, missing measurement conditions emerge as the main limit, as distinct records become indistinguishable without full context. We outline directions for the field, including shared physics rule libraries and self-reporting databases.

item.title: Optical Thermometry in Monolayer WS2: Raman and Photoluminescence Spectroscopy from 5 K to 1273 K
item.description: arXiv:2610.35214v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reliable temperature measurement is essential for characterizing and engineering two-dimensional (2D) semiconductor devices, yet optical thermometry of 2D materials has so far been demonstrated only over narrow temperature windows spanning a few hundred kelvin. Here, we establish a comprehensive optical thermometry framework for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K. We show that: (i) the out-of-plane A1g Raman mode shifts linearly with temperature above 100~K, with a slope of -0.0138 cm^{-1}/K in non-encapsulated WS2 (fitted over 298-1223~K) and a measurably smaller slope of -0.0121 cm^{-1}/K in an hBN-encapsulated sample (fitted over 100-1273~K); (ii) photoluminescence spectra measured over the same 5--1273~K range provide an independent optical indicator of the temperature: the neutral-exciton emission redshifts continuously with temperature and is well described by the semi-empirical P\"assler model. The two indicators probe distinct physical mechanisms, lattice anharmonicity and bandgap renormalization, and together provide contact-free thermometry for monolayer WS2 from 5~K to 1273~K, an approach applicable to 2D semiconductors more broadly.

item.title: Simultaneous suppression and temperature-driven crossover of particle-like and wave-like thermal transport in trigonal CsAg$_3$S$_2$
item.description: arXiv:2610.35360v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The simultaneous suppression of particle-like ($\kappa_p$ ) and wave-like ($\kappa_c$) thermal transport channels in crystalline materials remains a challenging problem, as reducing one channel can enhance the other. Here, we investigate the thermal transport in trigonal $P\Bar{3}m1$ CsAg$_3$S$_2$ using self-consistent phonon theory with cubic and quartic anharmonicity and the unified theory of thermal transport. Our calculations predict an ultralow lattice thermal conductivity of 0.222 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$ at 300 K, featuring simultaneously low $\kappa_p$ and $\kappa_c$ with a weak temperature dependence of $\sim$T$^{-0.42}$, which deviates significantly from the conventional $\sim$T$^{-1}$ behavior. This simultaneous suppression arises from localized Cs modes, which enhance anharmonic scattering, and the softer Ag-S framework, which reduces phonon group velocities, together suppressing $\kappa_p$, in conjunction with sparse, well-separated high-frequency S-derived optical modes that suppress $\kappa_c$ by limiting the coherent coupling between the phonon modes. Furthermore, the dominant transport channel exhibits a temperature-dependent crossover, with $\kappa_p$ contributing $\sim$74 \% of total lattice thermal conductivity at 300~K and $\kappa_c$ contributing $\sim$63 \% at 700~K. Combining the ultralow thermal conductivity with electrical transport calculated within the momentum relaxation time approximation (MRTA), we obtain a $ZT$ of 1.28 for $n$-type doping at 700 K. The present work not only clarifies the microscopic mechanism of ultralow thermal conductivity in trigonal CsAg$_3$S$_2$ but also identifies the covalent M-Ch framework modification within the AM$_3$Ch$_2$ family of ternary chalcogenides as an additional tuning parameter for further reducing $\kappa_p$ within the bonding-hierarchy design principle.

item.title: High-efficiency solid-state electrochemical thermal switching through phonon engineering of 2D materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.35547v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reversible solid-state thermal switches with large thermal contrasts remain rare, yet are essential for advanced thermal management. Using universal machine-learned interatomic potentials (uMLIPs) and density functional theory (DFT), we screen 57 transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDCs), spanning the 1T and 2H phases with Li and Mg intercalation. Among the candidates, Li$_a$ZrS$_2$ combines exceptional thermal conductivity switching with low heat capacity. Lithiation to Li$_{0.125}$ZrS$_2$ reduces the cross-plane thermal conductivity from approximately 3.7 to 0.05 W m$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$. The switching behaviour exceeds that of previously reported solid-state electrochemical thermal switches. Device-level modelling further demonstrates the potential for waste-heat recovery, with a pulsed system capturing 86\% of the energy recovered by an ideal switch. We attribute the switching behaviour to substantial softening of the Zr--Zr framework, with the mean force constant decreasing from approximately 4.2 to 1.2 eV $\mathrm{\mathring{A}}^{-2}$, alongside enhanced scattering of heat-carrying acoustic phonons. These findings establish electrochemical intercalation as a promising route to engineering thermal transport in layered materials.

item.title: MatOS: An Agent Operating System for Materials Research
item.description: arXiv:2610.34203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials research relies on scattered and growing data, knowledge, and simulation tools, and a single study often spans multi-day workflows across literature analysis, computation, and experiment. Large language model agents can now retrieve materials data, operate simulation codes, and close design-synthesis-characterization loops with autonomous laboratories. However, extending these agents with new capabilities, keeping long-running tasks on track, and letting them learn from past tasks and user feedback remain difficult. Here we present MatOS, an agent operating system for materials research with three core components: (1) a layered scientific asset graph that organizes data, knowledge, tools, skills, roles, and workflows as reusable assets; (2) a stateful adaptive workflow that runs tasks as explicit execution graphs with scientific checks, so that they can be resumed and traced; and (3) evidence-driven asset evolution, which revises these assets from execution records and user feedback. On ResearchClawBench, MatOS improves on the previously best-performing agent by 11.15% with the same base model and extends the cost-score Pareto frontier. With a common base model, it outperforms Codex CLI and Claude Code, exceeding Codex CLI by 2.13% on MatTools and 4.17% on SciAgentGym. In eight research cases, MatOS narrowed more than 30 million candidate structures to 97 solid-electrolyte candidates, identified 89 halide variants with higher computed conductivity than their parent structures, linked the force errors of 11 pretrained interatomic potentials to local atomic environments, and supported two new methods that reduce errors by 3.1% and 13.6% relative to their baselines. These results show that organizing research capabilities as reusable, evolving assets enables agents to carry out long, multistage materials studies. Code is available at https://github.com/DingyangLyu/MatOS.

item.title: Boundary-condition independence of infinite-chain ground states in the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic chain
item.description: arXiv:2610.34330v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extending the analytic machinery and using the numerical inputs from OpenAI's proofs of the Haldane gap, we study infinite-chain ground states of the $S=1$ $J$-$D$ antiferromagnetic model $H=\sum_j\{\boldsymbol S_j\cdot\boldsymbol S_{j+1}+D(S_j^{\mathrm z})^2\}$ for sufficiently small $|D|$. We consider two finite-volume settings: periodic chains with an even number of sites, and open chains with an odd number of sites and the same positive magnetic field in the $\mathrm z$ direction at both endpoints. We prove that the ground states in each setting have an infinite-chain limit along the full sequence, without passing to a subsequence, and that the two limiting states coincide. Convergence is uniform in $D$ on a fixed neighborhood of zero. The common limit is a symmetric locally-unique gapped ground state, and its local expectation values depend continuously on $D$. These conclusions concern the two specified constructions, not uniqueness among all infinite-chain ground states. They provide the input for the study of a topological phase transition in a forthcoming revision of our companion paper. The author formulated the problem and proposed the basic strategy. ChatGPT Astra made substantial contributions to the inductive estimates and to completing the proof.

item.title: Generative AI in Turbulence: Foundations, Applications, Validations and Benchmarks
item.description: arXiv:2610.35123v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI offers new approaches to turbulence problems in which incomplete observations or unresolved d.o.f. admit multiple physically plausible solutions. Potential applications include stochastic closures, super-resolution, data assimilation, uncertainty quantification, and the generation of Eulerian and Lagrangian flow ensembles. However, turbulence is not a conventional image-generation problem. Its multiscale dynamics, intermittency, extreme events, rough velocity fields and intrinsically stochastic transport make visual realism, pointwise error, and low-order spectral agreement insufficient measures of physical fidelity. We examine where generative AI provide novel capabilities with emphasis on diffusion models, score-based methods, and related probability-transport formulations. We discuss their use in unconditional generation, probabilistic reconstruction, reduced-order modeling, temporal evolution, and mesh-free representations. We argue that validation must address turbulence properties: energy transfer, structure functions, anomalous scaling, pdf tails, coherent structures, conservation laws, temporal consistency, ensemble diversity and generalization. Finally, we discuss potential limitations in validation, baseline, data availability and reproducibility, and the need for a benchmark ecosystem combining open data, standardized challenges, hidden tests, physics-aware metrics, and documented failures. This paper serves as a bridge between two communities. For AI practitioners, we provide a fair and accessible introduction to turbulence, essential for appreciating the challenges posed by the field and for assessing the physical relevance of generative models. For turbulent practitioners, we provide an introduction to the key technological aspects of Generative AI, clarifying what these tools actually do, and where their potential and current limitations lie.

item.title: Revealing the proton slingshot mechanism in solid acid electrolytes through machine learning molecular dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2503.15389v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In solid acid electrolytes CsH$_2$PO$_4$ and CsHSO$_4$, the origin of fast proton conduction has long been debated, attributed either to local proton hopping or to polyanion rotation. However, the precise role of polyanion rotation and its interplay with proton hopping remained unresolved. Nanosecond-scale molecular dynamics simulations, driven by equivariant neural network force fields, reveal a nuanced proton slingshot mechanism: protons are first carried by rotating polyanions, followed by O-H bond reorientation, and the combined motion enables long-range jumps. This mechanism challenges the conventional revolving paddlewheel model, revealing long-range transport arises from significant O-H bond reorientation assisted by only limited polyanion rotation. Despite their structural similarity, CsH$_2$PO$_4$ and CsHSO$_4$ exhibit qualitatively different transport behavior, governed by their distinct proton concentrations. In CsH$_2$PO$_4$, two rotation rates with different activation energies emerge, while CsHSO$_4$ displays a single-rate process with faster productive polyanion dynamics. The higher proton concentration in CsH$_2$PO$_4$ frustrates PO$_4$ rotation, resulting in slower dynamics than for SO$_4$ in CsHSO$_4$. In CsH$_2$PO$_4$, we further identify a unique correlation between oxygen sharing and proton transport, arising from the extra proton per polyanion. Together, our findings establish a unified framework linking polyanion rotation, proton coordination, and long-range transport, and suggest that tuning proton concentration could accelerate rotation and enhance conductivity.

item.title: CrystalREPA: Transferring Physical Priors from Universal MLIPs to Crystal Generative Models
item.description: arXiv:2605.08960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Crystal generative models mainly learn what stable crystals look like, with little explicit supervision for what makes them stable. We reveal a substantial representation gap between state-of-the-art crystal generative models and pretrained universal machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) via energy probing, and show this gap can be closed by a simple training-time alignment. We propose Crystal REPresentation Alignment (CrystalREPA), a plug-and-play framework that aligns the atom-wise hidden states of generative encoders with frozen MLIP representations through an element-aware contrastive objective, transferring stability-aware atomistic priors with marginal training overhead and no additional inference cost. Across three generative frameworks, ten MLIP teachers, and two benchmark datasets, CrystalREPA consistently improves the thermodynamic stability, structural validity, and structural fidelity of generated crystals. Equally important, we find that an MLIP's transfer effectiveness is poorly predicted by its accuracy on standard leaderboards (e.g., Matbench Discovery) but strongly predicted by the distinguishability of its atom-wise representation space, yielding a practical, accuracy-independent criterion for selecting MLIP teachers for generative transfer. Code is available at https://github.com/Chengqian-Zhang/CrystalREPA.

item.title: Raman Signatures of Lithium Ion Dynamics in LLZO Garnet Electrolytes: Atomistic Insights from MD-Raman Calculations
item.description: arXiv:2608.04690v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Lithium lanthanum zirconate (LLZO) garnets are among the most promising solid electrolytes for next-generation batteries owing to their high ionic conductivity, chemical stability, and compatibility with lithium metal. Raman spectroscopy is commonly employed to distinguish the highly conductive cubic phase from the poorly conductive tetragonal phase of LLZO, yet the atomistic origin of these spectral differences and their direct connection to Li-ion transport remain unresolved. Here, we close this gap by comparing computed and experimental Raman spectra for the tetragonal, cubic, and Ta-doped variants of LLZO, with the computed spectra obtained from the MD-Raman approach that combines machine-learning molecular dynamics with first-principles polarizability calculations. We show that the contrasting ionic transport behavior across these LLZO variants is encoded in the vibrational dynamics of the lithium sublattice and gives rise to distinct features in their Raman spectra. A symmetry-resolved analysis further reveals that experimentally observed Raman peaks do not correspond to individual normal modes, but instead arise from overlapping contributions of multiple symmetry channels, challenging conventional peak-assignment approaches. By explicitly connecting experimentally accessible Raman signatures to the underlying atomic-scale dynamics, our results show how Raman spectroscopy can move beyond empirical phase identification toward a microscopic probe of Li-ion dynamics in lithium garnet electrolytes.

item.title: Gap-controlled thermalization in a chain of alternating nonlinear springs: an SSH model version of the Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou problem
item.description: arXiv:2609.09498v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In classical anharmonic lattices, the resonance structure driving nonlinear mode mixing is reshaped by band gaps. However, it remains unclear whether a spectral gap hinders or promotes long-time thermalization. Here we study a Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou (FPUT) chain of equal masses joined by alternating dimensionless spring constants $1\pm\Delta\kappa$, so that the chain is dimerized with strength $\Delta\kappa$, the classical vibrational analogue of the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model, and quantify how the acoustic-optical gap controls relaxation under $\alpha$-type (cubic) nonlinearity. Tracking modal energies and spectral entropy via long-time symplectic simulations, we find that dimerization delays long-time relaxation. At $\Delta\kappa=1/2$, set by the onset of the first umklapp process that allows two zone-boundary acoustic phonons to fuse into a zone-center optical phonon, the three-wave acoustic-acoustic-optical channel closes. The effective acoustic-to-optical scattering rate reveals an interplay between the dynamic resonance vertex and the kinematic resonance manifold, which evolve differently with the dimerization parameter. Above the threshold $\Delta\kappa=1/2$, energy redistribution can nevertheless continue through higher-order resonances and quasiresonances. Yet specific boundary conditions and initial conditions can inhibit equipartition. These results identify the phononic gap as a tunable, momentum-selective filter for nonlinear energy transport, suggesting a general route to controlling energy transfer and equipartition in dimerized or topologically gapped nonlinear lattices and in flexible mechanical systems.

item.title: Reticulating Local Dynamics in Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
item.description: arXiv:2610.24418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In covalent organic frameworks (COFs), the geometry of the building units predetermines the structure of the framework, yet comparable design principles relating the COF linkers to the local motions that govern guest adsorption and diffusion as well as mechanical response have remained beyond reach. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function (PDF) analysis with molecular dynamics (MD) simulations accelerated by machine learning interatomic potentials to resolve and compare the local dynamics of two three-dimensional imine-linked COFs, chosen to differ in the geometry and rigidity of one of their two building units. Both are constructed from the same 4-connected square planar linker, $4,4',4'',4'''$-(pyrene-1,3,6,8-tetrayl)tetraaniline (PyTTA), reticulated with the 12-connected nanographene hexakis{[3,5-bis($p$-formylphenyl)-4,6-dimethoxyphenyl]}hexabenzocoronene to give COF-412, {[(HBC-LA$_{12}$)(PyTTA)$_3$]}$_{\mathit{imine}}$, and with the 6-connected triptycene 2,3,6,7,14,15-hexakis(4-formylphenyl)triptycene to give COF-564, {[(Trip-CHO)$_2$(PyTTA)$_3$]}$_{\mathit{imine}}$. The PDF-MD approach resolves the amplitude, the time scale, and the spatial extent of the motion of all COF linkers, separating the limited libration of the fused aromatic cores from the larger reorientational tilts of the pendant aryl rings they carry and from the translation of whole linkers within the net. The simulations further reveal that exchanging the nanographene- for the triptycene-based linker tunes the equilibrium tilt and the positional probability density of PyTTA, raising the tilt amplitude of its linker partner, and, notably, strengthens the coupling between the translations of neighbouring linkers. This approach provides a blueprint for understanding local dynamical properties in COFs, and shows them to be selectable through the choice of building unit and amenable to design.

item.title: Decoding Composition-Structure-Performance Relations in Sodium Layered Oxide Positive Electrode Materials
item.description: arXiv:2610.30591v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Layered sodium transition-metal (TM) oxides, Na$_x$TMO$_2$, are among the most promising sodium-ion positive electrode materials, yet their Na/vacancy orderings, layer stacking sequences, and cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions are known only for a few single-TM compounds. We compile the Na/vacancy orderings reported in earlier studies into a single library of 41 unique orderings and apply this uniformly to five single-TM and all ten Na$_x$TM$_{0.5}$TM$'_{0.5}$O$_2$ oxides (TM = Ti, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni), screening more than 120,000 structures with machine-learning interatomic potentials prior to 1,025 accurate first-principles calculations. The phase diagrams explain the observed O3/P3/O1 sequences and voltages, and the O3-to-P3 competition hinges on ordering energies of a few meV per atom that scalar descriptors, such as the cationic potential and the interlayer-slab distance, miss. Our extensive analysis reveals that the redox couples form a nearly partner-independent ladder, Ti$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Mn$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Co$^{3+/4+}$ $<$ Ni$^{2+/3+}$ $<$ Fe$^{3+/4+}$, explaining pristine charge transfer and the oxidation sequence. Van Vleck analysis of every TMO$_6$ octahedron reveals that TM mixing suppresses the cooperative Jahn--Teller distortions of Mn$^{3+}$ and Ni$^{3+}$ through charge transfer to Jahn--Teller-inactive states or dilution of Jahn--Teller-active centers. We formulate an energy-density-versus-strain map that yields a design rule: a high-voltage couple without Jahn--Teller strain, which Mn$^{4+}$/Ni$^{2+}$ charge transfer realizes in Na$_x$Mn$_{0.5}$Ni$_{0.5}$O$_2$, the most practical composition. We release the ordering-resolved dataset as a training set for subsequent training of accurate machine-learning interatomic potentials.

item.title: Machine learning kinetics from molecular dynamics data
item.description: arXiv:2609.17736v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Most molecular transitions occur on time scales far beyond direct molecular dynamics simulations. The committor, the probability that a configuration reaches a product state before a reactant state, is a central kinetic statistic, providing a mechanism-independent reaction coordinate and a foundation for transition path theory and the calculation of rates. This review surveys modern approaches for estimating the committor and related kinetic statistics from molecular simulations, with an emphasis on self-supervised methods that learn solutions of their defining dynamical equations rather than relying on labeled shooting data. We develop a common operator viewpoint connecting generator-based partial differential equations, variational principles, Markov state models, dynamical Galerkin approximation, and neural networks. Empirical and theoretical evidence points to the efficiency of these methods. We provide theoretical and practical guidance for realizing their full potential in applications, including strategies for treating non-Markovian effects and for sampling. We conclude by identifying opportunities for further research, including connections to reinforcement learning and generative modeling.

item.title: Hierarchical Response Theory of Electronegativity from Atomic Mean Inner Potential
item.description: arXiv:2610.29765v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Electronegativity remains conceptually ambiguous: is it a fixed atomic constant, or does it depend on the chemical environment? We resolve this debate by recasting electronegativity as a continuous response function rooted in the Atomic Mean Inner Potential (AMIP). Building on the established static scale \(\chi_{\mathrm{AMIP},1/2}\), we expand the electronegativity in fractional positive charge \(\delta\). The first-order term defines the Electrostatic Rigidity \(\mathcal{R}\), whose sign indicates whether an atom hardens or softens upon oxidation, and the second-order term defines the Electrostatic Anharmonic Modulus \(\mathcal{A}\). A logarithmic-derivative decomposition separates \(\mathcal{R}\) into an intrinsic, scale-independent response asymmetry \(\mathcal{D} \equiv \mathcal{R}_\Omega/\Omega_0 - \mathcal{R}_f/f_0\), which governs the competition between electronic screening loss (softening) and geometric volume collapse (hardening). Applying this to all 102 elements reveals a systematic dichotomy between softening main-group elements and hardening d-block elements, two scaling laws within the transition series, and two anomalies at half-filled d\(^5\) configurations and in Ce. The framework resolves the Cs--Fr controversy through relativistic analysis, reproduces classical electronegativity scales and Lewis acidity trends, and provides three falsifiable experimental predictions. It transforms electronegativity into a predictive, hierarchically structured quantum descriptor.

item.title: Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
item.description:
Nature Materials, Published online: 27 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41563-026-02775-4

The microscopic origin of ionic memory in two-dimensional (2D) nanofluidic memristors remains debated. Voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of 2D nanofluidic channels is identified to trigger memristive hysteresis leading to nonlinear ion transport in the channels.

item.title: Physical insights into the potential-dependent Na + transport in SnO 2−x alloying-type anodes for Na-ion micro-batteries
item.description: The modern world of microelectronics necessitates cost-effective, durable, high-performance micro-batteries. Na-ion micro-batteries with conversion-alloy-based anodes undergo phase transitions that modify their structural properties, affecting Na+ transport and making them difficult to probe. Here, we investigate Na+ transport in defect-engineered SnO2−x thin films deposited via radio frequency sputtering. Using cyclic voltammetry, the galvanostatic intermittent titration technique, and the distribution of relaxation time (DRT) derived from electrochemical impedance spectroscopy, along with ex situ scanning electron microscopy (SEM), we assess the interfacial and bulk Na+ kinetics. DRT-derived resistance reveals the breathing effect of the solid electrolyte interface layer and the evolution of electronic properties, resulting in lower total interfacial resistance at 0 V during cycling. Ex situ SEM images at the 1st, 100th, 650th, and 5000th cycles demonstrate that the activation process proceeds with pulverization induced by chemo-mechanical stress. These findings will help improve the performance of Na-ion micro-batteries undergoing complex conversion-alloying process.

item.title: Elucidating thermodynamic infeasibility of the (de)-lithiation process in 5V-class LiNi0.5Ge1.5O4 solid electrolyte
item.description: LiNi0.5Ge1.5O4 (LNGO), a Ge-substituted analogue of high-voltage cobalt-free LiNi0.5Mn1.5O4 (LNMO) spinel cathode, has previously been reported to show electrochemical inertness up to 5V vs. Li+/Li. However, thermodynamic and electronic origins of this inert behaviour have remained unexplored. Herein, we investigated the redox mechanism and thermodynamic driving force governing the (de)intercalation behaviour of LNGO using first-principles density functional theory (DFT+U) and verified using experimental findings. Convex hull analysis over the compositional range (0<2 in LixNi0.5Ge1.5O4) reveals absence of stable or metastable intermediate phases, supporting electrochemical inert behaviour. This was further reinforced by substantial evolution of structural symmetry, lattice parameters, and electronic band gaps during the process of (de)lithiation, resulting in a high-voltage stability up to 5 V vs. Li+/Li. Moreover, AIMD and CI-NEB calculations predicted Li-ion migration via vacant octahedral sites with a moderately high activation barrier of 0.537 eV. Experimental techniques such as linear sweep voltammetry, electrochemical impedance analysis and chronoamperometry were used to confirm DFT findings. These findings suggests that LNGO can be used as a possible solid electrolyte candidate in high energy density battery applications.

item.title: Revisiting Percolation and Molecular Diffusion in Disordered Pore Networks
item.description: The relationship between pore network structure and molecular diffusion in disordered nanoporous materials remains unclear. Here, we revisit two methodological choices that may contribute to inconsistent structure–diffusion relationships in the literature: percolation characterization and inclusion of non-percolating pores in diffusivity calculations. Our rigorous benchmarks show consistent results from Zeo++ and Mofography but reveal biased characterization from PoreBlazer due to limitations in its algorithm. Molecular dynamics simulations further consolidate that initializing adsorbates in percolating pore networks is essential for reliable and robust calculations of molecular self-diffusivity. With these issues addressed, we re-examine structure–diffusion relationships for methane across four amorphous material classes. Symbolic regression identifies the percolating backbone fraction as a key, yet largely overlooked, topology-related descriptor that captures a common diffusion trend across classes. Further analysis supports the added predictive value of this new descriptor beyond conventional geometric descriptors in machine learning tasks. Our work provides a consistent methodological foundation and a complementary descriptor for diffusion prediction in disordered nanoporous materials.

item.title: Orochi: A Physics-Grounded Python Package for Pair Distribution Function Analysis of Crystalline and Low-Dimensional Materials
item.description: Atomic pair distribution function (PDF) analysis from X-ray total scattering is a powerful methodology for determining atomic structure and arrangements across crystalline, disordered, nanostructured, and low-dimensional materials on both laboratory and synchrotron instruments. Fundamentally, PDF analysis relies on two core pillars—PDF data reduction from one-dimensional (1D) total scattering profiles and real-space structural modeling—often accompanied in rapid-acquisition experiments by upstream two-dimensional (2D) detector image processing. However, conventional workflows remain fragmented across disconnected software tools, forcing researchers to manually combine multiple programs and preventing the simultaneous optimization of measurement reduction parameters and crystal structure parameters that is standard in X-ray Rietveld refinement. Furthermore, mainstream PDF modeling engines rely on legacy physical approximations: they enforce three-dimensional (3D) periodic boundary conditions (requiring artificial vacuum supercells for 2D nanosheets), treat atomic scattering factors as angle-independent constants (causing peak distortions in compounds with large atomic number contrast), and approximate number density baselines using macroscopic bulk volume assumptions. Here, the open-source, pure-Python architecture of Orochi (version 4.0) is presented, implementing physical calculations from scratch in Python (accelerated via Numba) to unify total scattering data reduction, symmetry-aware crystallographic modeling, and real-space PDF simulation alongside a dedicated high-Q 2D detector processing module within a self-contained Python environment. Originally developed for laboratory total scattering studies of pharmaceutical glasses and deployed as compiled executable (β-version) tools at SPring-8 beamlines, Orochi has been completely redesigned around an externalized parameter management core (orochi.base) in which parameters are stored in standardized Python dictionaries and accessed via hierarchical string addresses. By bringing parameters outside the calculation engines rather than locking them inside built-in optimizers, this architecture allows multiple module instances across data reduction and structural modeling to be optimized simultaneously by modern optimization algorithms, machine learning libraries, and autonomous AI agents. For structural simulation, intra-cell atomic pair vectors are decoupled from lattice translation vectors to natively support arbitrary periodic boundary conditions across 3D crystals, 2D nanosheets, 1D nanowires, and 0D clusters. The simulation engine incorporates the full scattering vector (Q) dependence of atomic form factors, enabling accurate modeling of heavy/light-element oxides and permitting direct instrumental calibration using standard CeO2 powder rather than monoatomic nickel substitutes. Furthermore, a sinc-convolution density formulation is established to accurately reproduce baseline ripples arising from finite Qmin cutoffs in nanostructured systems. Complete mathematical formulations for all reduction and simulation algorithms are consolidated to establish a rigorous foundation for automated crystallographic analysis.

item.title: Phonon evidence for a partial, re-entrant spin reorientation near room temperature in LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31725v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spin reorientation near room temperature offers a route to controlling antiferromagnetic order, yet LaFeO$3$, which lacks a magnetic rare-earth ion, is generally expected to retain its spin orientation along the $a$ axis below $T{\mathrm N}\approx740$~K. Here, we investigate LaFe$_{1-x}$Ni$_x$O$_3$ ($x=0$ and 0.1) using temperature-dependent magnetization and Raman spectroscopy over 200--400~K. Both compositions exhibit magnetic anomalies at 285.6 and 323~K, respectively, accompanied by correlated deviations of 12 Raman modes from their conventional anharmonic behavior. Principal component analysis and a global fitting approach reveal a common temperature-dependent phonon response, with mode-dependent amplitudes and signs. To interpret these anomalies, we develop a Landau-based spin-phonon coupling model describing complete, partial re-entrant, and incipient spin reorientation. Comparison with the experimental Raman profiles favors a partial, re-entrant rotation of the N'eel vector in both compositions, centered near 290~K. Ni substitution narrows the characteristic reorientation interval from approximately 116 to 84~K and enhances the magnetization anomaly by a factor of four. An additional feature near 262~K in LaFeO$_3$ is consistent with the Morin transition of trace $\alpha$-Fe$_2$O$_3$. These findings suggest that partial spin reorientation can emerge without magnetic rare-earth ions and establish collective Raman phonon anomalies as a sensitive indirect probe of magnetic anisotropy changes in orthoferrites.

item.title: Unifying Low-Frequency Raman and Infrared Signatures across Perovskites
item.description: arXiv:2610.31830v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Perovskites have been studied for a wide range of applications, from oxide-based ferroelectrics to halide-perovskite photovoltaics. Despite their diverse functionalities, these materials share strong lattice anharmonicity arising from structural instabilities such as polar off-centering and octahedral tilting. These anharmonic distortions strongly influence the low-frequency vibrational response and can be observed in infrared (IR) and Raman spectra. However, low-frequency IR and Raman signatures are typically investigated separately, hindering the development of a unified understanding of vibrational spectroscopy across perovskite classes. In this work, we use machine-learning-based molecular dynamics to simulate the IR and Raman spectra of oxide perovskites (SrTiO$_3$ and BaTiO$_3$), halide perovskites (CsPbBr$_3$, CsSnBr$_3$, and CsGeBr$_3$) and double halide perovskites (Cs$_2$AgAlBr$_6$ and Cs$_2$AgBiBr$_6$). By comparing materials exhibiting polar, tilt-driven and mixed instabilities, we find that polar off-centering leads to enhanced low-frequency IR and dielectric responses, whereas nonpolar modes, particularly octahedral tilting, are associated with Raman central peaks. The strength of the low-frequency features also depends on how strongly the underlying modes couple to polarization or dielectric susceptibility. Finally, we show that the dynamics of these instabilities play an important role, with slow polar reorientations shifting the dielectric response to very low frequencies and overdamped tilting modes producing persistent Raman central peaks. These results establish a unified framework connecting low-frequency IR and Raman spectra to the symmetry, coupling and dynamics of their underlying anharmonic lattice instabilities.

item.title: Sub-monolayer tracking of molecular states at buried interfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.31924v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Phenomena responsible for emerging technologies originate from novel molecular states at buried interfaces. Yet quantitatively resolving these features is out of reach in most cases. Resonant scattering has demonstrated sensitivity to these local states but is limited due to a lack of accurate interpretive models. We leverage a machine learning (ML)-optimized optical model to analyze polarized resonant soft X-ray scattering (RSoXS) from molecular thin films. This new analysis establishes the direct and quantitative interpretation of molecular orientation, chemical identity and packing states as a function of depth with sub-monolayer resolution - reaching beyond the diffraction limit via locking energy and polarization through the optical model. From our analysis, we discover a gradient evolution of molecular orientation and packing emerging from the interface, indicative of competing surface versus bulk growth dynamics and contradicting hypotheses of substrate patterning. This nondestructive insight into buried interfacial formation and final state opens possibilities in controlling interfacial states and phenomena in next-generation technologies.

item.title: Strain-tunable van Hove singularity and superconducting dome in monolayer kagome metal CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$
item.description: arXiv:2610.32359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The recently discovered titanium-based kagome metal CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$, which exhibits superconductivity without an accompanying charge density wave, provides an ideal platform to investigate the intrinsic electronic structure and superconductivity. Moreover, it enables the exploration of superconductivity in the two-dimensional limit of the kagome lattice. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of biaxial mechanical strain ($\varepsilon$) on the electronic structure and superconductivity of monolayer CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$ using first-principles calculations. We demonstrate that the prominent van Hove singularity (VHS) at the M point can be monotonically tuned to the Fermi level by tensile strain. Furthermore, the superconducting transition temperature $T_C$ exhibits a dome-shaped dependence on strain, reaching a maximum of 3.6 K at an optimal tensile strain of $\varepsilon=+2\%$. The average superconducting gap magnitude is 0.35 meV, with an orbital-dependent and anisotropic distribution. Our results provide a detailed understanding of the superconductivity of monolayer CsTi$_3$Bi$_5$ and show that strain is an effective, continuous tuning knob for manipulating the electronic structure and superconductivity.

item.title: Machine Learning Accelerated Simulation of Charge Regulation Effects
item.description: arXiv:2610.32713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many solvated materials, from nanoparticles to polyelectrolytes, acquire charge through the dissociation or association of surface groups, a phenomenon known as charge regulation (CR). Recent methods use hybrid charge regulation Monte Carlo (CR-MC)/molecular dynamics (MD) to evolve the system while dynamically adjusting charges on the surface groups. However, this approach is computationally expensive, as Monte Carlo sampling can be as costly as the accompanying MD. In this work, we introduce charge regulation machine learning (CR-ML), a graph attention network that predicts the ionization probability of every surface site from the instantaneous configuration, the dissociation constant of surface groups, and the solution conditions. We show that CR-ML reproduces the equilibrium conformations and degree of ionization obtained with CR-MC for a hydrophobic polyanion. We further test CR-ML on the more complex system of two nanoparticles mediated by a polyelectrolyte, where it accurately predicts the charge asymmetry that develops between the two particles. Across these systems, CR-ML updates charges an order of magnitude faster than CR-MC while accurately reproducing its equilibrium properties. This framework opens a path toward large-scale simulations of charge-regulating materials for understanding and designing their responsive behavior.

item.title: Generalization properties of the token perceptron: the role of embedding and vocabulary
item.description: arXiv:2610.32788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are trained to predict tokens from a finite vocabulary, each represented by a vector in a $d$-dimensional embedding space. Therefore, token prediction is a classification problem whose classes have a geometry determined by the embedding. We study how this geometry affects learning in a minimal solvable model: a linear predictor that maps a sequence of $N$ embedded tokens to a $d$-dimensional output through one $d\times d$ matrix per position, trained in the teacher--student setting. We call this the \textit{token perceptron}. We compute its generalization error with the replica method, taking $N\to\infty$ at fixed number of examples per position $\alpha=P/N$ and keeping $d$ and the vocabulary size $D$ finite. As a first reference case, we consider continuous embeddings on the sphere, which isolate the role of the embedding dimension. The natural load is then $\alpha/d$, and for $d>1$ a normalized label fixes the direction of the teacher output, so the problem becomes a noiseless regression: the teacher is recovered exactly above $\alpha_{\rm rec}=d^2/(d-1)$, and spherical cross-entropy reaches this threshold at large inverse temperature. In the same setting the storage capacity of random associations scales as $d^2$ for margins $O(1/\sqrt{d})$. We then turn to vocabulary embeddings, where a label only identifies the Voronoi cell of the teacher output, so that each example imposes inequalities rather than equations, as in the classical perceptron. We compute the Bayes-optimal error for a given embedding matrix through an approximate spectral closure and show that the optimal learner first resolves the directions in which the vocabulary has the largest variance, even when the teacher is isotropic.

item.title: Combining Simulations and Spectroscopy to Design Protective Coatings on Sulfide Solid Electrolytes
item.description: arXiv:2610.32905v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sulfide solid electrolytes are attractive for all-solid-state batteries because of their high Li-ion conductivity and favorable processability, but their practical use is limited by electrochemical instability and moisture-induced degradation. Molecular surface coatings offer a scalable strategy to improve humidity tolerance and interfacial stability, yet there is limited understanding of the molecular-level factors governing surface interactions. By combining large-scale atomistic simulations enabled by a machine-learning potential with targeted experiments, we present a comprehensive framework for designing molecular coatings on Li$_6$PS$_5$Cl (LPSCl). Using a PET-MAD interatomic potential fine-tuned on an r$^2$SCAN reference dataset covering LPSCl surfaces, molecular adsorbates, and their interactions, we model surface adsorption of carboxylic (CA), sulfonic (SA), and phosphonic (PA) acids with alkyl chains of varying lengths and the interaction of these coated surfaces with water at finite temperature. The simulations show that lithiated head groups generally exhibit more favorable adsorption energies. Impedance spectroscopy shows that the lithiated coatings maintain 40--55\% of the initial ionic conductivity after powder processing. While adsorption strength is largely controlled by head-group chemistry and lithiation state, coating morphology depends primarily on alkyl-chain length and surface coverage. In particular, long-chain lithiated carboxylates form dense, brush-like hydrophobic layers that reduce water access to reactive Li surface sites, with protection setting in at a coating thickness of approximately 0.8 nm. Consistent with these predictions, longer carboxylate chains suppress H$_2$S evolution more effectively. Because thicker coatings also hinder Li-ion transport, intermediate chain lengths offer the best balance between moisture protection and ionic conductivity.

item.title: From Heterogeneity to Function: Enhanced Modular Dynamic Range in Hierarchical Brain Networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.32328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hierarchical and modular organization defines brain architecture, yet how it supports flexible computation and functional specialization remains unclear. Although dynamic range is a hallmark of efficient information processing, its distribution across modules and hierarchical levels remains largely unexplored. Here, we show that hierarchical-modular networks naturally generate heterogeneous modular dynamics and firing rates, extending regimes of critical-like dynamics with enhanced intrinsic timescales, reflecting critical slowing down, and diverse scaling exponents without fine-tuning near criticality. Intrinsic timescales increase across hierarchical levels, while their dispersion within levels emerges only when connectivity profiles and firing rates are heterogeneous. We introduce modular dynamic range to quantify how individual modules respond to external inputs and show that heterogeneity enhances both global and module-specific sensitivity, with modular intrinsic timescales increasing with dynamic range. Local stimulation reduces dynamic range in homogeneous networks but enhances it in heterogeneous networks relative to global stimulation. Moreover, selectively stimulating intermediate hierarchical levels maximizes both global and modular dynamic range, revealing a principle of functional specialization. In heterogeneous networks, modular dynamic range is more variable and increases even in unstimulated modules, demonstrating distributed computational benefits beyond directly stimulated regions. Together, these findings establish heterogeneity as a mechanism through which hierarchical-modular networks sustain critical-like dynamics, generate hierarchical timescales, and distribute computational sensitivity, providing a basis for functional specialization without fine-tuning to criticality.

item.title: Kagome goldene with flat bands and Dirac nodal line fermions via line-graph epitaxy
item.description: arXiv:2503.07945v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The kagome lattice has emerged as a promising platform for investigating exotic quantum phases. However, achieving a single-atomic-layer kagome lattice in elemental materials remains a significant challenge. Here, we introduce line-graph epitaxy, a novel approach that enables the atomic-scale synthesis of goldene, a monolayer of elemental gold atoms arranged in a kagome lattice. Through scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS), and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we demonstrate the formation of kagome goldene, featuring a flat band with a van Hove singularity approximately 1.1 eV below the Fermi level, signaling strong electron correlation effects. Notably, the flat band is disrupted at the zigzag edges of goldene nanoflakes, revealing substantial edge effects. Furthermore, our calculations show that weak interlayer interactions between goldene and the underlying Au2Ge substrate generate dual Dirac nodal lines through a proximity effect. These findings offer not only a novel strategy for constructing elemental kagome lattices, but also a generalizable framework for fabricating and controlling line-graph materials. This research advances the exploration of quantum phases driven by strong correlations and the design of materials for next-generation quantum technologies.

item.title: AtomMOF: All-Atom Flow Matching for MOF-Adsorbate Structure Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2602.07351v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising materials for applications such as direct air capture, where performance depends on how adsorbates bind within the framework. Accurately predicting MOF-adsorbate configurations is therefore important for screening candidate materials. However, traditional approaches are computationally expensive and require a known host structure, while existing generative models rely on rigid-body assumptions and do not explicitly model adsorbates. We introduce AtomMOF, a scalable all-atom flow-matching model that jointly predicts MOF-adsorbate structures from discrete building blocks and adsorbates. Built on a Diffusion Transformer with a building block-based pairwise attention bias, AtomMOF operates in an unconstrained all-atom space and exhibits clear scaling behavior. To improve the structural validity of flexible all-atom models, we also propose Feynman-Kac (FK) steering with machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs). On the BW dataset, AtomMOF achieves a 58.17% relative increase in match rate and a 31.84% relative reduction in RMSD compared with prior work. MLIP-guided steering further improves validity by 28.7% and reduces formation energy error by 86.5%. On ODAC25, AtomMOF generates adsorption configurations faster than GCMC and, when combined with MLIP relaxation, identifies lower-energy configurations than those in the reference dataset.

item.title: Realization of a Synthetic Hall Torus with a Topological Charge Pump in a Spinor Bose-Einstein Condensate
item.description: arXiv:2602.14549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report the first experimental realization of a synthetic Hall torus using a spinor Bose-Einstein condensate confined in a ring-shaped trap with in situ imaging. By cyclically coupling three hyperfine spin states via Raman and microwave fields, we impose a periodic boundary condition in the synthetic dimension, which, together with a real-space ring trap, realizes a toroidal geometry with synthetic magnetic flux penetrating the surface. This flux induces azimuthal density modulations whose periodicity is uniquely determined by the quantized toroidal flux, a hallmark of the Hall torus. We then implement a topological charge pump by adiabatically varying an axial flux through the torus, inducing quantized azimuthal transport of the atoms. We further investigate the onset of these modulations as the system transitions from cylindrical to toroidal topology. Our results establish a versatile platform for exploring quantum Hall physics and topological phenomena in synthetic curved spaces.

item.title: Machine Learning Assisted Design of Complex and High Entropy Alloys by Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD Process for Low Carbon Energy Applications in Extreme Environments
item.description: arXiv:2608.01903v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Complex and high entropy alloys are attracting much attention currently thanks to their mechanical and corrosion resistance properties in harsh environments, in particular needed for carbon-free energy applications. However, their elaboration in bulk and in thin film form in a trial-and-error approach is impractical due to their complexity and the cocktail effect. The recent development of artificial intelligence brings a new possibility for their elaboration and adjustment of their properties. Firstly, we present an overview of Materials and data science research. Then we describe how DIADEM - French initiative for Materials and Data science convergence - tackles the development of innovative coatings for carbon-free energy applications (nuclear, high temperature electrolysis, ...) thanks to the development of a nationwide network of synthesis and characterization platforms - the DIADEM discovery hub. We describe in particular DIADEM-2D, an AI-driven Hybrid HiPIMS/Pulsed-DC PVD process using 4 cathodes in confocal combinatorial configuration. We present the high entropy alloy determination using data from the literature for corrosion resistance in molten salt media and nuclear accidental conditions. An element-independent model gathering deposition parameters and coating properties has been implemented allowing the design of protective coatings with a particular composition. We demonstrate the feasibility of this process and its accuracy.

item.title: An LLM agent for end-to-end computational materials discovery
item.description: arXiv:2608.20434v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Coordinating multi-scale tasks is an effective strategy for computational materials discovery, yet the diverse algorithms and tools involved make this process highly challenging. Here we present DREAMS, a large language model (LLM)-based agent system capable of executing the entire screening pipeline for metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). DREAMS processes a large body of MOF literature, links publications to their crystal structures, and curates them into a computation-ready database, which is then screened with progressively more expensive simulations. The promising candidates identified for separation under wet flue gas conditions all originate from independent studies. By bridging the heterogeneous stages from literature mining to high-throughput simulation, DREAMS operates across application domains and enables even non-experts to discover high-performance materials in an end-to-end, automated manner.

item.title: Unmodeled states and uncertain action outcomes in agentic scanning tunneling microscopy
item.description: arXiv:2609.27302v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In physical experiments, interventions can alter hidden experimental states in ways that cannot be predicted in advance. Autonomous scientific agents must therefore interpret the consequences of their interventions while operating with incomplete knowledge of the experimental state. Here we investigate this problem using scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) tip conditioning, traditionally a human-expert-intensive task governed by inaccessible tip apex conditions and uncertain action outcomes. We introduce quailbot, an agent harness that places the LLM inside the instrument feedback loop by linking physical interventions with experimental readbacks. After a brief apprenticeship with a human expert, frontier LLM agents autonomously completed end-to-end tip conditioning on an STM and passed an independent verification. The contingencies that arose during the experiments further exposed the limits of LLM agentic autonomy when relevant experimental states or dynamics were hidden or unmodeled. Our results show that future autonomous physical experimentation requires agents to infer hidden and unmodeled experimental states, track the outcomes of their actions, and operate within the observability and action limits of real instruments.

item.title: Testing Transformer Learnability on the Arithmetic Sequence of Rooted Trees
item.description: arXiv:2512.01870v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study whether a transformer network can learn the deterministic sequence of trees generated by the iterated prime factorization of the natural numbers. Each integer is mapped into a rooted planar tree and the resulting sequence $\mathbb{N}\mathscr{T}$ defines an arithmetic text with measurable statistical structure. A transformer network (the GPT-2 architecture) is trained from scratch on the first $10^{11}$ elements and evaluated on next-token prediction and masked-token prediction tasks, with a Hidden Markov Model as baseline and a scaling analysis over context window, dataset size, vocabulary size and model size. The model reaches a word accuracy of about $0.4$, well above the baseline, and its performance remains stable on test blocks located at $10^{13}$-$10^{15}$, far beyond the training interval. Moreover, the likelihood assigned by the trained model separates the arithmetic text from two controls: synthetic token sequences that preserve the marginal token frequencies but not their order, with a separation that widens with the context, and sequences containing more than three consecutive square-free integers, a configuration that arithmetic forbids. These results indicate that the transformer captures regularities of the arithmetic text that go beyond its frequency profile.

item.title: Neural networks become centroid classifiers when trained on heavily corrupted inputs
item.description: arXiv:2606.11319v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Learning from imperfect data is a central theme in machine learning, connecting practical questions of robustness to fundamental questions of learnability. Here we examine attribute noise: learning from corrupted inputs while keeping the labels intact, a setting that has received considerably less analytical attention than its label-noise counterpart. We consider two types of corruption models: additive noise and replacement noise. Through experiments with multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) on corrupted classification datasets, we find that neural networks remain robust, maintaining well-above-chance accuracy even when inputs are >90% corrupted -- far beyond human recognition. To understand this robustness, we analyze infinite-width networks in the heavy-corruption regime using a mean-field-inspired approach and derive a leading-order decision rule for the classification outcome: the network implements a prototype rule, the nearest-class-mean, assigning each test point to the class whose training-set average it most closely resembles. This leading-order decision rule is universal across a broad range of MLP architectures, holding for any depth, as well as a wide class of activation functions and noise distributions. The same centroid mechanism closely matches finite-width network behavior in our experiments and provides an interpretable and analytically tractable account of why learning can succeed even when individual training examples carry almost no signal.

item.title: Contrastive Regularization of Machine Learning Potentials
item.description: arXiv:2606.31660v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Machine learning models are increasingly trained as regressors and then deployed as generators, from language models to learned simulators. In this setting, accuracy on held-out data says little about the distribution a model produces when it is sampled. We study this problem where the correct distribution is fixed by first principles, in machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) trained by minimizing the mean squared error (MSE) on density functional theory (DFT) energies and forces, then used to run molecular simulations. The MSE never constrains the Boltzmann distribution that the potential defines, so an MLIP can match held-out DFT data and still drift, when sampled, into spurious minima that corrupt its thermodynamics. Building on the variational principle of statistical physics, we introduce Contrastive Regularized MSE (CRMSE), a post-training step in which the potential acts as its own energy-based model and learns to reproduce the distribution it generates, without any new DFT data. On molecules from the MD17 benchmark, CRMSE restores physical sampling and recovers DFT free-energy profiles, while keeping energy and force errors within chemical accuracy. Our results suggest that a model meant to be sampled must be trained on the distribution it produces, not only for pointwise accuracy.

item.title: Expanding the galactose oxidase substrate repertoire via a multi-modal computational strategy
item.description: Computational chemistry; Protein; Bioengineering; Biocatalysis; Structural biology; Machine learning

item.title: Regulating carrier transport and oxychloride interphase formation by increasing configurational complexity in solid-state halide electrolytes
item.description: Cost-effective Li2ZrCl6 halides with regulated configurational complexity combine rapid lithium-ion conduction with ultralow electronic conductivity and superior oxidative stability. A robust zirconium oxychloride cathode-electrolyte interphase is formed during cycling, enabling 4.4 V all-solid-state LiNi0.85Co0.1Mn0.05O2 batteries to operate for up to 3,700 cycles.

item.title: From Bench to Game Engine: An Instructor-Built Suite of 3D Laboratory Simulations Created with Generative AI
item.description: Virtual chemistry laboratories have historically required either a commercial subscription or a software development team, placing custom simulations out of reach for most instructors. I report the design and construction of a suite of browser-playable 3D laboratory simulations for a non-science-majors chemistry course that has no formal laboratory component — density of an unknown metal, pH of common solutions, double replacement reactions, separations by paper chromatography, and physical and chemical changes — that I built alone in the Unity game engine, with no prior game-development experience, using a large-language-model coding assistant connected directly to the engine. Each lab pairs a 3D fume hood, rendered by a Unity WebGL build, with an HTML worksheet that checks readings, assigns per-student unknowns, and prints a one-page report; the answer data lives in the compiled build rather than in the page, so students cannot read it from the source. The labs serve two purposes: laboratory experience for students who would otherwise have none, and continuity of instruction when hurricane closures disrupt the weekly schedule. I describe the development workflow, the division of labor between instructor and AI, the design decisions that keep the simulations chemically honest, the time and cost involved, and the limitations encountered. All builds, worksheet pages, and prelab reviews are freely available on GitHub. The approach offers a reproducible path for instructors to author their own laboratory simulations: the five described here were built in about one month.

item.title: Adapting UMA to spin-polarized AQCat25 without catastrophic forgetting with task-gated LoRA
item.description: Universal models for atoms such as UMA rival specialized interatomic potentials across chemistry [2], yet none of their catalysis datasets contains spin-polarized metallic surfaces [4, 9, 10]. On AQCat25 [1], a spin-polarized, higher-fidelity catalysis dataset, UMA loses accuracy where adsorption changes surface magnetization, and fine-tuning risks catastrophic forgetting [8, 13]. We add a task-specific mode to UMA through low-rank adapters (LoRA) [5] that act only on AQCat25 systems (0.065% of parameters). On unseen adsorbates and materials, the adsorption-energy error falls from 0.193 to 0.119 eV (−38%) and the force error from 0.091 to 0.031 eV/Å, with the largest gains on strongly magnetic systems. All seven original UMA tasks remain numerically unchanged, whereas full fine-tuning raised the OC20 error tenfold. EV2-in+midFiLM [3], the best model in the AQCat25 paper, reaches 0.268 eV on the same systems. Rather than predicting adsorption energies directly, UMA derives them from total energies, as the AQCat25 authors recommend for surfaces that restructure [1]. A foundation potential can thus gain a spin-aware, higher-fidelity mode without forgetting what it already knows.
